title: Build tool failing from disk space exhaustion caused by unrotated logs
notes: Tool failure -> root cause (log rotation not configured) -> fix -> verification, mirroring the fx06 tool-failure shape with a different scenario.

turns.text: The build server is failing every job now with 'ENOSPC: no space left on device' during the compile step.

Let me check disk usage on the build box... /var/log is at 94GB, almost entirely build-agent.log which has been growing unbounded since the agent was installed 8 months ago — log rotation was never configured for it.
Can we just delete the old log to unblock builds right now?
Yes, truncating build-agent.log now to free space immediately — that should unblock builds right away while we fix rotation properly.

Added a logrotate config for build-agent.log: daily rotation, compress, keep 14 days, so it can never grow unbounded again. Also added a disk-space check to the build agent's health check so future exhaustion fails loudly with a clear message instead of a cryptic ENOSPC mid-build.
Ran three consecutive build jobs after the fix — all completed successfully, and disk usage on /var/log dropped to under 2GB after truncation and stayed flat across the three runs.

gold_atoms.text: build-agent.log had grown unbounded to 94GB over 8 months because log rotation was never configured for it, eventually exhausting disk space and failing every build with ENOSPC.

Add a logrotate config for build-agent.log (daily rotation, compress, keep 14 days) so it cannot grow unbounded again.
Add a disk-space check to the build agent's health check so future exhaustion fails loudly with a clear message instead of a cryptic mid-build ENOSPC.
Verified the fix by running three consecutive build jobs successfully; /var/log usage dropped to under 2GB and stayed flat across the runs.
